extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, health insurance issuers, and other stakeholders (e.g., HHS reviewers, policy commenters)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts regulatory criteria and standards governing State Exchange participation in the SEIPM program, improper payment classification and enforcement, user fee rates for FFEs and SBE-FPs, EHB definitions (particularly dental), and multi-year catastrophic plan rules for the 2027 benefit year and beyond.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEIPM satisfaction of duplicative programmatic audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A State Exchange's participation in SEIPM would satisfy certain duplicative annual independent external programmatic audit requirements, particularly the review of compliance with provisions of subparts D and E that may result in improper payment of APTC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If finalized, HHS would issue sub-regulatory guidance identifying which programmatic audit requirements could be satisfied through completion of SEIPM for a given plan year. Policy rationale: reduce burden on State Exchanges while maintaining audits for requirements not reviewed as part of SEIPM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper payment classification principle (§155.1650(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would classify APTC payments as improper when a State Exchange failed to provide adequate documentation demonstrating that such payments were made in accordance with applicable Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with Federal improper payment measurement standards under the PIIA requiring classification as improper when insufficient documentation exists to determine payment propriety. The burden of providing adequate supporting documentation rests with State Exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining substantial noncompliance (§155.1650(b)(1)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS would determine a State Exchange failed to substantially comply with SEIPM if one or more specific measurable criteria are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed measurable criteria include: (1) failure to submit required data or documentation within the timelines specified in the Annual Program Schedule; (2) submitting data or documentation found to be incomplete, inaccurate, or in a format that would reasonably prevent effective review; (3) failure in the CAP process; and (4) a pattern—more than five instances during a SEIPM cycle—of non-response within 30 calendar days to HHS requests for clarification or additional information. The compliance framework focuses on substantial failures that materially affect improper payment measurement rather than minor technical violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on substantial versus minor violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance criteria would focus on substantial compliance failures that genuinely impact the integrity and effectiveness of SEIPM rather than minor technical violations that would not materially affect improper payment measurement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is intended to balance clear, enforceable standards with recognition of complex State Exchange operations and occasional operational challenges; ensures data quality sufficient for reliable measurement results while preserving collaborative relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to cure before remedial measures (§155.1650(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Before implementing remedial measures, HHS would provide written notice to the State Exchange specifying the nature of the noncompliance and the potential consequences and allow a reasonable opportunity to cure or demonstrate compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cure period would be set commensurate with the complexity of the compliance issue. The notice and cure provision promotes collaborative problem-solving and provides clarity on deficiencies and potential consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial measures framework (§155.1650(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS could implement measures or procedures to secure State Exchange compliance if failures undermine or prohibit HHS' efficient administration of Exchange improper payment measurement activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed remedial measures include: (1) enhanced monitoring and reporting; (2) mandatory implementation of specific operational procedures or controls; and (3) on-site visits to State Exchange facilities to assess operations, data systems, and compliance. The approach is graduated and tailored to the nature and severity of noncompliance, enabling targeted technical assistance and oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation of State Exchange authority (§155.1650(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS could initiate proceedings to revoke a State Exchange's authority to operate if the State Exchange continues to fail to comply after implementation of initial remedial measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation would be reserved for cases where other remedial measures failed and continued operation poses unacceptable risks to program integrity and enrollee protection; represents the most serious enforcement action available.

rubrics_metrics.name: FFE user fee rate and remittance requirement for 2027 (§156.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed FFE user fee rate for the 2027 benefit year: 2.5 percent of total monthly premiums. Participating issuers offering plans through an FFE must remit a user fee equal to the product of the annual user fee rate specified in the annual HHS notice and the monthly premium charged for each policy where enrollment is through an FFE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale and methodology: rate based on estimated costs, enrollment (including anticipated transitions among Exchange models), and premiums. Issuers participating in an FFE receive special benefits (e.g., QHP certification, ability to sell coverage to individuals determined eligible for QHPs). HHS may revise rates for the final rule if operational costs, enrollment, or premium projections materially change.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBE-FP user fee rate and remittance requirement for 2027 (§156.50)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed SBE-FP user fee rate for the 2027 benefit year: 2.0 percent of total monthly premiums. Issuers offering a plan through an SBE-FP must remit a user fee equal to the product of the monthly user fee rate and the monthly premium charged for each policy where enrollment is through an SBE-FP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SBE-FP fee is calculated based on the proportion of total FFE costs associated with Federal activities that provide SBE-FP issuers with special benefits (estimated at ~80%). Methodology uses the same assumptions as FFE (budget, enrollment, premiums) and may be updated for the final rule if projections change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitting plan-level adjustments for multi-year catastrophic plans (§156.80(d)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §156.80(d)(2)(ii) to permit issuers of multi-year catastrophic plans to make plan-level adjustments to the index rate that reflect the length of the entire term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments would account for plan design characteristics (deductible, maximum out-of-pocket). Any calculation of the magnitude of the plan-level adjustment must be accurate and actuarially justified. HHS seeks comment on whether and to what degree term-based adjustments are permitted above other plan design adjustments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause on review of State EHB-benchmark plan selections (§156.111)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS is pausing review of State applications to select EHB-benchmark plans in accordance with §156.111 while conducting a comprehensive review of section 1302 of the Affordable Care Act and considering future rulemaking to revise §156.111 and other EHB regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States should note the pause and ongoing comprehensive statutory/regulatory review when planning EHB benchmark submissions or related state-level changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including routine non-pediatric dental services as an EHB (§156.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to revise §156.115(d) to prohibit issuers from including routine non-pediatric dental services as an EHB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: interpretation of section 1302(b)(1) and (b)(2)(A) — the 10 EHB categories explicitly include pediatric oral care, implying non-pediatric dental services were not intended as EHBs; 'typical employer plan' interpreted as the employer's major medical plan (not the whole suite of benefits). KFF survey data show dental is often provided as a separate product. The proposal would not prevent States from addressing non-pediatric oral health via non-EHB mandates. Operational impacts discussed: coding (CDT), provider networks, cost-sharing, effects on SADPs, and potential premium/HSAs implications. The typicality quantitative test remains unchanged (states may include value of such services in actuarial comparisons but may not include them as EHBs). HHS seeks comment on impacts across markets and plan types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of 2027 parameters in guidance (§156.130(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For benefit years where methodology is unchanged, publish the premium adjustment percentage index (PAPI), maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, reduced maximum annual limitation on cost sharing, and required contribution percentage in guidance annually by January preceding the benefit year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 2027, methodology finalized in the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability final rule (using private health coverage premiums excluding Medigap and certain accident insurance) remains in effect; parameters for 2027 are published in guidance rather than included in this rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year catastrophic plan term and benefit design options (§§156.130(c) and 156.155(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to specify that a catastrophic plan may have a plan term of either 1 year or multiple consecutive years not to exceed 10 years, and issuers of catastrophic coverage may enroll individuals for multi-year terms up to 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed allowances: catastrophic plans with terms of at least 2 years may utilize value-based insurance designs to offer preventive services under section 2713(c) of the PHS Act without requiring the enrollee to first satisfy deductible or annual cost-sharing. HHS requests comment on whether issuers of multi-year catastrophic plans should apply the annual limitation on cost sharing on an annual basis or on average over the life of the contract.
